name: The Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology (TBSRTC)
specimen: Thyroid FNA (US-guided or palpation), smears, LBC, cell block
use: All thyroid FNA specimens in adults and children.
Lymph node FNA for suspected metastatic thyroid carcinoma can use the same terminology (with Tg washout).
Every report should begin with one of the six category names (numbers optional but recommended alongside the name).
not_use: Non-thyroidal neck masses (use Milan for salivary, Sydney for lymph node).
Parathyroid lesions intentionally sampled (report descriptively + PTH washout).
report_structure: Specimen and site/nodule (side, size, TI-RADS if provided)
Diagnostic category name (± number), e.g. 'Benign (Bethesda II)'

adequacy.title: Adequate
items: At least 6 groups of well-visualised follicular cells, each with ≥10 cells, preferably on a single slide.

Exceptions (adequate regardless of count): solid nodules with cytologic atypia (any significant atypia → report it); solid nodules with inflammation (e.g. lymphocytic thyroiditis, abscess, granulomatous thyroiditis); colloid nodules with abundant thick colloid (benign).
Cell block/LBC can contribute to cellularity.

adequacy.title: Nondiagnostic
items: Below threshold; cyst fluid only (macrophages); blood only; obscuring artefact; poor fixation/staining.
Two consecutive ND results: correlate with US; consider core biopsy or surgery if suspicious.

categories.name: Nondiagnostic
categories.definition: Specimen does not meet adequacy criteria (except exceptions listed) or is uninterpretable because of preparation artefact.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Repeat FNA with ultrasound guidance (no minimum wait required). Persistently ND solid nodules: close follow-up or surgery.
criteria: Fewer than 6 groups of ≥10 well-preserved, well-stained follicular cells.
Poorly prepared, poorly stained or obscured follicular cells (blood, thick smears, air-drying).
Cyst fluid only (macrophages ± few cells) – report as ND, 'cyst fluid only' and correlate with US (purely cystic, no worrisome features may be followed).

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – insufficient follicular cells
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I). Insufficient follicular epithelial cells for evaluation.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – cyst fluid only
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I) – cyst fluid only.
diagnoses.comment: Only macrophages/cyst contents are present without adequate follicular cells. Correlate with ultrasound; repeat FNA of any solid component is recommended if clinically/radiologically indicated.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – blood only / obscured
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I). Specimen consists predominantly of blood; follicular cells are scant/obscured.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

diagnoses.name: Nondiagnostic – poor preservation/air-drying artefact
diagnoses.final: Nondiagnostic (TBSRTC Category I) due to air-drying/preparation artefact.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA with optimal smear preparation/fixation is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category I – Nondiagnostic

categories.name: Benign
categories.definition: Benign follicular nodule, thyroiditis or other benign finding.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Clinical and sonographic follow-up; repeat FNA only if growth or suspicious US features.
criteria: Benign follicular nodule: adequate follicular cells in flat sheets/macrofollicles, honeycomb, abundant colloid; macrophages; no significant atypia.
Abundant thin/thick colloid with few cells is acceptable as benign.
Thyroiditis: lymphoid cells ± oncocytes (Hashimoto), granulomas (subacute), neutrophils (acute).

diagnoses.name: Benign follicular nodule (adenomatoid/colloid nodule, nodular goitre)
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Consistent with a benign follicular nodule.
diagnoses.comment: Smears show abundant colloid and benign follicular cells in flat sheets with macrophages. Clinical and ultrasound follow-up recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Graves disease (diffuse hyperplasia)
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Benign follicular cells, consistent with Graves disease in the appropriate clinical context.
diagnoses.comment: Flame cells/marginal vacuoles may be present; correlate with thyroid function tests and antibodies.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Chronic lymphocytic (Hashimoto) thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Consistent with chronic lymphocytic (Hashimoto) thyroiditis in the proper clinical context.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid cells with oncocytic follicular cells. Correlate with anti-TPO/anti-Tg antibodies. If a dominant monotonous lymphoid population is present, flow cytometry is advised to exclude lymphoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Subacute granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Consistent with granulomatous (de Quervain) thyroiditis.
diagnoses.comment: Epithelioid granulomas and multinucleated giant cells engulfing colloid with degenerated follicular cells; clinical correlation (painful gland, raised ESR) recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Acute (suppurative) thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Acute suppurative thyroiditis.
diagnoses.comment: Neutrophils, necrotic debris and macrophages. Culture is recommended; consider pyriform sinus fistula in children.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Riedel thyroiditis / IgG4-related thyroiditis
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II) – scant fibrous stromal fragments with few inflammatory cells; findings may be compatible with Riedel (IgG4-related) thyroiditis in the right context.
diagnoses.comment: Aspirates are often scant/nondiagnostic; biopsy and IgG4 correlation needed.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Benign cyst / cystic degeneration with follicular cells
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). Benign follicular nodule with cystic change.
diagnoses.comment: Macrophages, colloid and adequate benign follicular cells. Follow-up recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

diagnoses.name: Black thyroid / amyloid / other benign
diagnoses.final: Benign (TBSRTC Category II). [Specify benign finding].
diagnoses.comment: Correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category II – Benign

categories.name: Atypia of undetermined significance (AUS)
categories.definition: Cells with architectural and/or nuclear atypia not sufficient for FN, SFM or malignant. 3rd ed: single term AUS (FLUS removed); subcategorize as AUS-nuclear or AUS-other.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Repeat FNA, molecular testing, diagnostic lobectomy or surveillance. Paediatric: repeat FNA or surgery (molecular testing not established). Lab AUS rate should be ≤10%.
criteria: AUS-nuclear: focal nuclear atypia (enlargement, pallor, grooves, irregular contours) in otherwise benign aspirate; extensive but mild atypia; atypical cyst-lining cells; 'histiocytoid' cells.
AUS-other (architectural): prominent microfollicles/crowding in a sparse aspirate insufficient for FN.

AUS-other: predominance of oncocytic cells in sparse aspirate with scant colloid; atypical lymphoid cells (flow recommended); atypia not otherwise categorised (e.g. psammoma bodies without PTC nuclei).
Recommended: specify subtype in report; nuclear atypia carries higher ROM.

diagnoses.name: AUS – nuclear atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-nuclear (cytologic atypia).
diagnoses.comment: Focal nuclear changes (enlargement, pallor, grooves) are present but insufficient for suspicious for PTC. Repeat FNA and/or molecular testing is suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – architectural atypia (microfollicles)
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other (architectural atypia).
diagnoses.comment: Scant aspirate with predominant microfollicles insufficient for follicular neoplasm. Repeat FNA and/or molecular testing is suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – nuclear and architectural atypia
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-nuclear and architectural.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA, molecular testing or diagnostic lobectomy as clinically appropriate.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – oncocytic cell predominance (sparse)
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other (oncocytic cells).
diagnoses.comment: Sparse aspirate composed predominantly of oncocytic cells with scant colloid; clinical context (e.g. Hashimoto, multinodular goitre) may favour benign. Repeat FNA/molecular testing suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical lymphoid cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other (atypical lymphoid cells, lymphoma not excluded).
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA with material for flow cytometry is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical cyst-lining cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-nuclear (atypical cyst lining cells).
diagnoses.comment: Likely reactive cyst-lining cells but PTC cannot be excluded; repeat FNA of solid area suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

diagnoses.name: AUS – psammoma bodies without diagnostic nuclear features
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance (TBSRTC Category III) – AUS-other.
diagnoses.comment: Psammoma bodies without papillary carcinoma nuclear features. Repeat FNA suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category III – AUS

categories.name: Follicular neoplasm (FN)
categories.definition: Moderately to highly cellular aspirate of follicular cells with marked crowding/microfollicles, or composed exclusively of oncocytic cells (FN, oncocytic type). Includes cases with mild nuclear changes (to account for NIFTP/follicular-pattern tumours).

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Molecular testing and/or diagnostic lobectomy. Paediatric: surgery.
criteria: Cellular aspirate with predominant microfollicles/trabeculae, crowding and overlapping; scant colloid.
Mild nuclear changes (enlargement, chromatin pallor) allowed if no true PTC nuclei (papillae, pseudoinclusions absent).
FN oncocytic type: almost exclusively oncocytic cells (abundant granular cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli), few/no lymphocytes or colloid.

diagnoses.name: Follicular neoplasm
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV).
diagnoses.comment: Cellular aspirate of follicular cells in microfollicles with scant colloid. Differential includes follicular adenoma, follicular carcinoma, follicular-pattern PTC/NIFTP and adenomatous nodule. Molecular testing and/or lobectomy suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Follicular neoplasm, oncocytic (Hürthle cell) type
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm, oncocytic (formerly Hürthle cell) type (TBSRTC Category IV).
diagnoses.comment: Aspirate composed almost exclusively of oncocytic cells. Differential includes oncocytic adenoma/carcinoma and oncocytic hyperplastic nodule. Molecular testing and/or lobectomy suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Follicular neoplasm with mild nuclear changes (NIFTP/follicular variant PTC in differential)
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV). Mild nuclear changes are present.
diagnoses.comment: Differential includes NIFTP, invasive encapsulated follicular variant PTC and follicular adenoma/carcinoma. Lobectomy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

diagnoses.name: Hyalinizing trabecular tumour (favored)
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV), favouring hyalinizing trabecular tumour (or Suspicious for malignancy depending on nuclear features).
diagnoses.comment: Cohesive cells around hyaline material, grooves and pseudoinclusions; Ki-67 (MIB-1) membranous staining supports. Lobectomy suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm
diagnoses.note: HTT may be categorised as FN or SFM depending on features.

diagnoses.name: Parathyroid tissue (intrathyroidal) suspected
diagnoses.final: Follicular neoplasm (TBSRTC Category IV) – cannot exclude parathyroid tissue.
diagnoses.comment: Immunostains (GATA3, PTH, chromogranin; TTF1/Tg negative) or PTH washout measurement suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm

categories.name: Suspicious for malignancy (SFM)
categories.definition: Features strongly suspicious but insufficient for definitive malignancy. Specify: suspicious for PTC, MTC, lymphoma, metastatic, other.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Molecular testing, lobectomy or near-total thyroidectomy.
criteria: Suspicious for PTC: patchy nuclear changes, incomplete nuclear changes, sparse cells with PTC features, or cystic degeneration pattern.
Suspicious for MTC: monomorphic plasmacytoid/spindle cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin, insufficient material for IHC (calcitonin, CEA).
Suspicious for lymphoma: monomorphic lymphoid cells; flow cytometry needed.
Suspicious for malignancy, other (e.g. metastasis, ATC).

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Some nuclear features of PTC are present but are focal/incomplete. Molecular testing or surgery recommended; NIFTP is in the differential.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for medullary thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for medullary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Serum calcitonin and CEA, and calcitonin immunostain on repeat FNA/cell block, are recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat FNA for flow cytometry or core biopsy is recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for metastatic malignancy
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for metastatic [carcinoma/melanoma].
diagnoses.comment: Clinical history and IHC on cell block suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for malignancy, other (e.g. anaplastic carcinoma)
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy (TBSRTC Category V) – suspicious for [specify].
diagnoses.comment: Further sampling/biopsy recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category V – Suspicious for malignancy

categories.name: Malignant
categories.definition: Cytomorphologic features conclusive for malignancy; specify type.

rom.source: TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)
TBSRTC 3rd ed (Ali, VanderLaan, Baloch et al., Thyroid 2023;33:1039, doi 10.1089/thy.2023.0141)

categories.management: Lobectomy or near-total thyroidectomy (PTC/follicular-derived); MTC, ATC, lymphoma and metastases managed by tumour-specific protocols. Active surveillance may be an option for papillary microcarcinoma.
criteria: PTC: papillae/sheets, enlarged oval overlapping nuclei, pale powdery chromatin, grooves, intranuclear pseudoinclusions, psammoma bodies, ropy colloid, multinucleate giant cells.
MTC: dispersed plasmacytoid/spindle/round cells, salt-and-pepper chromatin, red cytoplasmic granules (MGG), amyloid; calcitonin+.
High-grade follicular-derived (poorly differentiated/DHGTC): insular/solid/trabecular, scant colloid, mitoses, necrosis.
ATC: markedly pleomorphic epithelioid/spindle/giant cells, necrosis, neutrophils.
Lymphoma, SCC, metastases.

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (classic)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Diagnostic nuclear features of PTC (enlarged overlapping oval nuclei, powdery chromatin, grooves and intranuclear pseudoinclusions) with papillary fragments and psammoma bodies.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, follicular subtype
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma, consistent with follicular subtype.
diagnoses.comment: Microfollicles with well-developed PTC nuclear features. NIFTP cannot be excluded cytologically for encapsulated lesions; histology required.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, tall cell subtype
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma, with features suggestive of tall cell subtype.
diagnoses.comment: Cells 2–3× taller than wide with abundant oncocytic cytoplasm and frequent pseudoinclusions; aggressive subtype – histological confirmation required.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, other subtypes (columnar, hobnail, diffuse sclerosing, Warthin-like, oncocytic, solid, cribriform-morular*)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – papillary thyroid carcinoma, [subtype] features.
diagnoses.comment: *Cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma is a separate entity in WHO 2022 (CTNNB1/APC; β-catenin nuclear positivity; consider FAP).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – medullary thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Confirmed by calcitonin positivity / elevated serum calcitonin. Recommend serum calcitonin, CEA, RET germline testing and pheochromocytoma screening.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated / high-grade follicular-derived carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – carcinoma, consistent with poorly differentiated (high-grade follicular cell-derived) thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Solid/insular/trabecular groups, scant colloid, mitoses and necrosis; TTF1/PAX8/thyroglobulin positive.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Anaplastic (undifferentiated) thyroid carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Highly pleomorphic malignant cells with necrosis. Urgent oncology referral; BRAF V600E testing recommended for targeted therapy.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of thyroid
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: WHO 2022 classifies primary thyroid SCC as a pattern of anaplastic carcinoma; exclude direct extension or metastasis (larynx, oesophagus).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma (e.g. DLBCL, MALT lymphoma)
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – non-Hodgkin lymphoma [type if determined].
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/IHC confirm; low-grade MALT lymphoma often needs histology.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Metastatic malignancy
diagnoses.final: Malignant (TBSRTC Category VI) – metastatic [carcinoma/melanoma], consistent with [primary].
diagnoses.comment: Common primaries: kidney, lung, breast, melanoma. IHC on cell block recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category VI – Malignant

diagnoses.name: Follicular / oncocytic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Not diagnosable on cytology – report as Follicular neoplasm (Category IV).
diagnoses.comment: Capsular/vascular invasion cannot be assessed on FNA.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: TBSRTC Category IV – Follicular neoplasm (not VI)
diagnoses.note: Included for search: follicular carcinoma is never Category VI on FNA.

extra.title: Paediatric notes (3rd ed)
items: ROMs are higher in children for every category (ND 14%, B 6%, AUS 28%, FN 50%, SFM 81%, MAL 98%).
Molecular testing is not yet standard; AUS → repeat FNA or surgery, FN → surgery (lobectomy/thyroidectomy).

extra.title: NIFTP impact
items: 3rd ed quotes ROM with NIFTP counted as malignant; where NIFTP is excluded, ROM falls (largest drop in FN, SFM, AUS).
Avoid diagnosing 'malignant – PTC' for purely follicular-patterned lesions with subtle nuclear changes; use SFM or FN.

extra.title: Molecular testing
items: Afirma GSC/XA, ThyroSeq v3, ThyGeNEXT/ThyraMIR are used for AUS/FN to refine risk (where available).

references: Ali SZ, VanderLaan PA (eds). The Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology: Definitions, Criteria, and Explanatory Notes. 3rd ed. Springer, 2023.
Ali SZ, Baloch ZW, Cochand-Priollet B, et al. The 2023 Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology. Thyroid. 2023;33(9):1039–1044.
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Tumours. 5th ed. IARC, 2022.
